sections.h2: Selling a Friendswood house for cash
sections.html:
In Friendswood you can take a cash bid, hire an agent, or ask the buyer to wait until you have moved. Cash fits a house that needs work, a short deadline or a cloudy title.

Friendswood is a residential suburb south of Houston, home to many who work in the space industry or in Houston. A well-kept house can do fine on the open market. A storm-damaged house or one stuck in an estate is what investors price fastest.

  • Find out how long each offer stays open and what could shift it after the buyer's inspection.
  • Settle who pays for title insurance, recording and any association transfer fees.
  • Get the buyer to name the title company and commit to a target date on paper.

Four creeks, Clear Creek among them, drain the land, so ask your insurer and the county about drainage history for your lot and tell buyers what you learn. Rank offers by what lands in your account after payoff, taxes and fees. That beats the headline price, particularly when one buyer wants repairs done and another does not.

The city straddles Galveston and Harris counties, which means taxes and records depend on where the county line cuts your parcel. Look at the deed or tax bill for the county name, and begin with that before phoning anyone.

Galveston Central Appraisal District covers the City of Friendswood and Friendswood ISD. The school district keeps its own tax assessor-collector, apart from the one for the city, so a Galveston County lot can receive bills from two collectors. Gather every payoff figure before closing.

If your lot is in the Harris County part, values come from the Harris County appraisal district instead. Ring that office, not the Galveston one, when you are on the north side.

Statements arrive near the start of October, and the last day to pay without a penalty is the end of January. Because the year's lien rides with the house, the closing agent pays what is owed out of your proceeds.

Texas collects no state property tax, so the local units on your bill set the amount. A value you think is too high can be contested before the appraisal review board.

Friendswood tax steps in order
StepTiming
Value setStart of each year
Notice of valueHomestead notices go first, in early spring
ProtestReview board hearings begin in mid-spring
Rate adoptedUnits adopt rates by late September
PaymentBills mailed in the fall

Each collector can tell you what has been billed and what remains.

Selling ends your homestead exemption. The buyer files separately for theirs. An older or disabled owner's school tax ceiling can travel to a replacement Texas homestead.

  • A disability rating can bring relief that scales with the rating and covers the whole homestead at 100 percent.
  • After the first exemption year, a homestead's appraised value is limited by a yearly cap.

Request the exemption list on your account from the appraisal district, and fix any error before you list.

Each situation has a workable route. A small estate affidavit or an affidavit of heirship can move an inherited house, though the title company wants different proof for each.

For a loan in default, the borrower can reinstate by paying what is past due within 20 days of the default notice. A sale ahead of the auction date lets you keep whatever equity exists.

If a tenant lives there, a buyer may accept the lease, or you can follow the written notice and justice court path. Tell buyers early which applies, so the bids reflect it.

Paperwork comes first, since it speeds up any route you pick. Buyers will ask for your deed, current tax statements from each collector, a mortgage payoff letter and owners association papers. The easiest way to dodge a last-minute delay is to collect each bill and payoff early.

  • Locate the legal description and verify the county on your tax bill.
  • See whether an old lien, judgment or unreleased deed of trust still sits in the records.
  • Write down repairs you know about, such as roof, plumbing or foundation items, and choose between fixing them and selling untouched.
  • Choose a closing window that fits your move.

A lot of Friendswood houses have been recorded and re-recorded for decades. Long chains of ownership occasionally hide a missing release or an unclear heir. Finding that early protects your schedule, so order a title search before signing and request the results in writing.

A buyer who pays cash removes the usual weak points of a mortgage sale. Nobody's bank can send an appraisal back low, nobody's loan can die the week before you move, and the post-inspection repair haggling mostly disappears. The house changes hands in whatever state it is in, and the calendar bends around your move rather than a lender's.

The price of that comfort is a smaller figure. Get each bid's net in writing, then hold it against a listing: subtract commission, fix-up costs, and every month you would keep paying the mortgage, utilities and tax while waiting for a buyer.

Once you say yes, the title company starts a file and combs the records for liens, judgments and tax balances. Whatever turns up gets cleared first. Then comes the signing, with a notary watching you execute the deed. Your lender is paid, the tax share is covered, and the remainder reaches your bank by wire.

Carry photo identification, house keys and any gate or garage openers. For an empty house, leave the utilities on until the buyer agrees to a date. Need a few extra days to finish moving? Request them before signing, and have the contract say so.

  1. Ask the lender for a payoff letter.
  2. Pull a tax statement from each collector named on your bill.
  3. Read the settlement statement the day before.
  4. Sign, then keep copies of every recorded paper.

Buyers in a creek-drained area will ask about water. Dig out any flood insurance paperwork, repair invoices for past leaks and photographs of the yard after heavy rain. Handing those over yourself looks far better than having an inspector discover the story. Pair them with the age of the roof, the water heater and the air conditioner, and your cash buyer can price the house without padding for unknowns.

Which county clerk files your deed, Galveston or Harris, depends on the parcel. The instrument must carry a notary acknowledgment before it is accepted.

Statute sets the fees and they can change, so verify with the clerk. The closing agent submits the paperwork and wires your net after lien payoffs clear.

faqs.q: Is Friendswood in Harris County or Galveston County?
faqs.a: Both. It sits in northwestern Galveston and southern Harris counties, so your tax bill shows which covers your lot.

faqs.q: How long does a cash sale take in Friendswood?
faqs.a: Title work and your payoff set the pace, and a written closing date from the buyer helps. Probate or lien cleanup adds time.

faqs.q: Does a Friendswood seller still owe tax after closing?
faqs.a: The year's lien rides with the property, and the title company usually pays what is due from proceeds. Ask each collector for a current statement.

faqs.q: Will a Friendswood buyer accept a house with repairs pending?
faqs.a: Yes. As-is buyers price in the repair cost, so set that offer beside a listing net after repairs and commission.

faqs.q: Does a Friendswood sale end my homestead exemption?
faqs.a: Yes. The exemption needs an owner who lives there, so the buyer files a new request.
